cues: The equations of angular motion mirror the linear ones.
v equals r omega links the two worlds, in radians only.
Rotational energy is half I omega squared, where I is the sum of m r squared.
A rod has M L squared over twelve about its centre and over three about its end.
Torque is r F sine phi, and equals I alpha.
Work is tau theta and power is tau omega.
And angular momentum, I omega, is conserved when no external torque acts.
text: Let us recap. The equations of angular motion mirror the linear ones. v equals r omega links the two worlds, in radians only. Rotational energy is half I omega squared, where I is the sum of m r squared. A rod has M L squared over twelve about its centre and over three about its end. Torque is r F sine phi, and equals I alpha. Work is tau theta and power is tau omega. And angular momentum, I omega, is conserved when no external torque acts.
